div.div:
1. echo "$ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"
If it prints angle brackets, the placeholders were
never replaced. Stop here.
2. curl the gateway directly. A body starting
{"id":"msg_ proves URL and credential.
An unknown-model error still proves both, because
the gateway authenticated before rejecting.
3. Run claude, then /status. An Anthropic
base URL row appears only when a gateway is set.
4. Send a prompt, then open Observability → Logs.
The row carries model, tokens, and cost. If the
prompt worked but no row appears, you are still
talking to Anthropic directly.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 434px; height: 1px; padding-top: 759px; margin-left: 482px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Where the values live, and which one wins

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 781px; margin-left: 484px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Shell exports live only in the terminal that ran them.
A Claude Code session started from any other window
uses the normal login and shows no base URL row. This
is the most common "it did not work" report.
~/.claude/settings.json makes it permanent for
every session. Add the three values inside an env
block; the file has to stay one JSON object.
Precedence
• Settings file beats shell export.
• ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN beats a saved claude.ai
login, which stays saved and unused.
• /status tells you which source is active, so use it
rather than guessing.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 434px; height: 1px; padding-top: 759px; margin-left: 947px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Two decisions to make before you roll this out

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 781px; margin-left: 949px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
1. Where the key is allowed to be written.
Never in a project's .claude/settings.json. That
file is committed and shared with everyone who clones
the repository. Use the user-level
~/.claude/settings.json, or the gitignored
.claude/settings.local.json for one project.
2. One key per developer, or one for the team.
A shared key makes Observability show one caller for
the whole team, and revoking it after a leaver takes
everyone offline at once. A key per developer gives
per-person cost and clean revocation, at the price of
issuing and tracking them.
Either way, put the person or team in the key's metadata
tags at issue time. That is the only thing the logs can
group by later.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1364px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1084px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Claude Code is only the worked example. Any client that accepts a base URL override follows the same pattern with no application logic change: the Anthropic SDK takes base_url and auth_token constructor arguments and also reads
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL from the environment, and the OpenAI SDK takes the same two through its own base_url argument. What changes is the endpoint and the credential. Nothing else.
